0.long_answer: The yellowish discoloration of the skin and sclera is called neonatal jaundice, a condition that occurs when there is an elevated level of bilirubin in a newborn's blood. This buildup of bilirubin is primarily due to the immaturity of the liver, which is not yet efficient at metabolizing and excreting bilirubin. As a result, the pigment accumulates, leading to the characteristic yellow appearance. Neonatal jaundice is common, affecting up to 80% of newborns in their first week of life. Although it is usually a benign condition, very high levels of bilirubin can lead to complications, such as acute bilirubin encephalopathy, requiring treatment interventions like phototherapy or exchange transfusions.
